dohori.basis: No source counts recordings; this is a judgement. Himal Southasian (2011) says dohori duets 'form the backbone of the commercial recording industry' in Nepal; the National Folk and Duet Song Academy has about 4000 member singers, composers and artists; English Wikipedia credits Raju Pariyar with over 16,000 songs and Bishnu Majhi with over 5,000, mostly lok dohori duets recorded to order at several a day. Commercial lok dohori on cassette and VCD from the 1990s and on YouTube since about 2010 is issued by hundreds of singers each year on small Kathmandu labels (Indreni Cassette Centre, Music Nepal, Ashish Music) that no catalogue lists in full, so even the low figure is uncertain; recorded field dohori is a tiny archival fraction. Many recordings are near-copies on the same tunes. An insider's essential list is about 40 songs.

tamangselo.basis: No source counts recordings; this is a judgement, not a count. What was read: Hira Devi Waiba, called the genre's pioneer, sang nearly 300 folk songs (Radio Nepal from 1966, HMV albums 1974 and 1978); Kathmandu cassette labels (Ranjana Music, Indreni Cassette Center, Music Nepal) issued Tamang selo albums from the 1990s on, several now on iTunes; established singers have a few selo albums each (Indira Gole Gurung: three); a damphu selo programme ran 100 episodes; and an iTunes US search for 'tamang selo' on 2026-11-23 returned more than 150 releases naming the genre, most of them single-track YouTube-era uploads from 2023-2026 (Raj Kumar Dong Tamang, Chitra Bahadur Tamang, Jivan Bomjan Tamang and others with a dozen or more each). Counting cassette-era albums, radio recordings and the stream of new singles gives a few thousand recordings; the high end allows for the large YouTube-only output. An insider's essential list is about 40: Hira Devi Waiba's early recordings, the 1990s pop-selo hits (Kunti Moktan's Mathi Mathi Sailungema), classic cassette selo singers and a handful of current stars.

pasillo.basis: No source counts pasillo recordings; this is a judgement, not a count. Pasillo has been recorded for over a century in two main countries (Ecuador and Colombia) and more thinly in Venezuela (as vals), Panama and Central America. English Wikipedia (citing Benavides) says that in 1911, 67 of the 272 pieces recorded in Ecuador were pasillos; Nicasio Safadi's Dúo Ecuador recorded Guayaquil de mis amores and 37 other songs on 19 discs in New York on 19 June 1930. Single composers left hundreds of pasillos (Francisco Paredes Herrera 219, Carlos Vieco 273), and Julio Jaramillo alone made more than 200 45 rpm discs from 1956 to 1960, besides LPs titled for pasillos. Colombian duets (Garzón y Collazos, 216 songs; Silva y Villalba; Dueto de Antaño) and string ensembles (Oriol Rangel) mixed pasillos with bambucos across dozens of LPs, and iTunes still shows a steady flow of new 'pasillo ecuatoriano' albums and singles (2020-2026). An insider's essential list is about 60 recordings, split between the Ecuadorian sung pasillo (Dúo Ecuador, Carlota Jaramillo, Benítez-Valencia, Julio Jaramillo, Olimpo Cárdenas, Miño Naranjo) and the Colombian vocal duets and instrumental pasillo fiestero.

meringue.basis: A judgement, not a count. What is on record: Issa El-Saieh's La Belle Créole label alone issued about 35 sides marked (Meringue) between 1947 and 1956 (French Wikipedia discography), alongside the other Port-au-Prince dance orchestras of the 1940s-50s; Folkways (Haitian Piano, 1952; Calypso and Meringues, 1953) and Remington (Emy de Pradines, Original Meringues, 1953) LPs; Seeco and French 78s of Haitian méringues; the 1936-37 Lomax field recordings; reissue compilations (Corason 1993, Frémeaux 2015, Ostinato 2016 still uses the label for 1960-1981 records); and a small art-music shelf of recorded piano and guitar méringues (Duroseau, Saintonge, Casséus). After the mid-1950s most Haitian dance records are filed as kompa rather than méringue, which caps the range. An insider's essential list is about 40 recordings, most of them 1937-1960 orchestra sides and salon piano pieces.

gaitazuliana.basis: A judgement, not a count; written before collecting. Gaita zuliana has been recorded commercially since the 1960s and every Christmas season brings new LPs, then CDs and singles, from dozens of Maracaibo conjuntos (Cardenales del Éxito, Guaco, Maracaibo 15, Saladillo, Gran Coquivacoa, Barra de Maracaibo, Estrellas del Zulia and many more), each with long discographies of 10-12-track albums; add several hundred newer groups and singers and the regional labels' catalogues. An insider's essential list is about 60 recordings: the classic gaitas of Ricardo Aguirre, the Cardenales, Guaco's early gaita years, Maracaibo 15 and Saladillo, plus a few standards such as 'La grey zuliana' and 'Sentir zuliano'.

pasodoble.basis: A judgement, not a count. No source counts pasodoble recordings. What was seen: Spanish Wikipedia says pasodobles are still composed in great numbers on the Levante coast for the Moros y Cristianos festivals, and SGAE found Paquito el chocolatero the most-performed live piece in Spain in 2007; iTunes Spain alone returns dozens of whole albums titled 'Pasodobles', 'Pasodobles Toreros', 'Pasodobles Taurinos' or 'Pasodobles Falleros' by municipal, military and festival bands (Banda Sinfónica Municipal de Madrid, Unidad de Música de la Guardia Real, Banda de la Plaza de Las Ventas, La Artística de Buñol, the Villena bands), each of 10-40 tracks, plus every copla singer of 1930-1970 (Estrellita Castro, Concha Piquer, Juanita Reina, Manolo Escobar) recording sung pasodobles, and compilations such as Warner's 30-track 'Pasodobles' (2020). Counting band repertoire recorded by hundreds of local bands since the 1920s (España cañí was first recorded in 1926) puts the total in the tens of thousands; the low figure counts only distinct commercially issued recordings. An insider's essential list: about 60, roughly 30 band pasodobles (taurino, militar, festero) and 30 sung pasodobles canción.

harana.basis: A judgement, not a count; no source counts recordings. Harana was sung live under windows, not made for records, and the practice has declined since the 1980s. What is on record: the 78s, radio and LP output of crooners such as Ruben Tagalog (a 12-track Villar Records 'Harana' collection) and Villar's Ilocano harana records by Felipe Alonzo; a handful of dedicated modern albums (Introducing the Harana Kings, 14 tracks, 2012; Florante Aguilar's The Art of Harana, 14 guitar serenades, 2003; Charmaine Clamor's My Harana, 12 jazz-leaning tracks, 2008); and a guitar series that mixes harana and kundiman (Raffy Lata, seven volumes, 2022-2026). Regional repertoires (Cebuano, Ilocano, Bicolano) add uncatalogued cassette and local releases. The many recent pop singles titled 'Harana' mostly are not the genre. An insider's essential list is about 30 recordings, most of them Ruben Tagalog and the Harana Kings.

jiangnansizhu.basis: Judgement made before collecting, not a count. The repertoire is small (the Eight Great Pieces plus a dozen or so other club pieces), but each piece has been recorded many times: by Shanghai amateur clubs, conservatory and state ensembles (Shanghai Conservatory, Zhejiang, Central Chinese Orchestra), China Record Company LPs and cassettes, Hong Kong and Taiwan labels (Hugo, ROI, Wind), and Western world-music labels (Ocora, Nimbus, Naxos, Smithsonian, Nonesuch). An insider's essential list is about 25 recordings: one or two good readings of each of the eight pieces plus Chunjiang huayue ye, Xing jie and a few club pieces.
